name: Grow garlic
blurb: Plant in autumn, forget about it, harvest in summer. Garlic is the lowest-effort, highest-satisfaction crop there is — and home-grown varieties beat supermarket garlic easily.
gear: Seed garlic from a supplier, not a supermarket bulb
A sunny well-drained bed or a deep pot
steps: Buy proper seed garlic — supermarket bulbs are often treated to stop sprouting and may carry disease.
Choose type by climate: hardneck for cold winters and better flavour, softneck for milder areas and longer storage.
Plant individual cloves in autumn, pointy end up, about 5 cm deep and 15 cm apart.
Leave it alone over winter. Garlic needs a cold period to form bulbs rather than a single round.
Snap off the flowering scapes on hardneck types in early summer and eat them — it puts energy into the bulb.
Harvest when the lower third of leaves have yellowed, then cure in a dry airy place for a few weeks before storing.
tips: Harvesting too late makes the bulbs split and store badly.
Garlic hates sitting wet. Raised beds or pots if your soil is heavy.
proof: A cured crop of proper bulbs that stores through winter in your kitchen.
